correctness.rationale: The fixed domain and n>=16 cutoff are explicit. For every directed cut of size k, invertible matrices form a block-triangular family of cardinality |GL_k(q)||GL_(n-k)(q)|q^{k(n-k)}; two-way cuts form block-diagonal families. These give the exact singleton terms. Summing all k=2,...,n-2 via the stated n>=16 geometric bound and bounding singleton overlaps using forbidden-entry counts gives the displayed universal 6κ and 5κ bounds. Their relative errors vanish uniformly, their ratio yields the conditional gap, and the connected-component recurrence is an exact partition of invertible matrices. Verification enumerated all GL matrices and all cuts in six field/size cases and reproduced the formulas. Finite checks do not prove the all-n bounds; the symbolic proof does.

value.rationale: The explicit 2026 random-evolution-algebra question motivates precise asymptotic simplicity and indecomposability. Two distinct rare matrix-support defects have different exponential orders under invertibility conditioning, producing a meaningful conditional probability gap. The exact labeled component formula recovers the full finite-size decomposition profile, not merely a particular arbitrary example; both results apply across all prime powers. Broader sparse/isomorphism-type models are explicitly outside scope.
